question.text: Kailash Opportunities Fund (Category II AIF, constituted as a Trust) has onboarded 950 non-accredited investors and wishes to raise further capital by adding 150 more LPs. Which of the following is CORRECT?

answer.text: Permitted — the Trust may have up to 2,000 investors per scheme
Permitted only with SEBI's specific waiver for each additional investor
Not permitted — each scheme of an AIF may have MAX 1,000 investors; accredited investors are EXCLUDED from this count
Permitted only if the fund converts to open-ended

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Reg 10(f) as amended by SEBI (AIF) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2025 (w.e.f. Nov 19, 2025), no scheme of an AIF shall have MORE than 1,000 investors. However, accredited investors are EXCLUDED from this count. For a Company structure, the Companies Act 2013 sub-cap is 200 investors in a private placement. Here, adding 150 non-AI LPs would breach the 1,000 cap (950 + 150 = 1,100). **The Trap:** Option A fabricates a 2,000 cap. Option B misstates the waiver process — the cap is hard. Option D conflates open/close-endedness with investor count. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests this with the same numbers. Earlier the cap was written differently before the 2025 amendment. For Companies Act structure, always apply the 200 Private Placement sub-limit. Mutual Fund (V-A) has no such investor cap. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Design your LP mix strategically — if you expect 800+ LPs, convert to LVF or AI-only format to uncap the count. Alternatively, run parallel schemes: Scheme-I and Scheme-II each can hold 1,000 investors. Document the rationale in the PPM.
